newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Ecuador's deposed leader seeks support in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's deposed leader seeks support in Argentina.

text.p: Ecuador's ousted President Abdala Bucaram, on a tour of Latin America to win support, arrived in Argentina on Thursday and denounced the "coup d'etat" that he said toppled him.
"I am going to legally expose matters and the whole world will understand that there is cowardice in being silent about a coup d'etat," Bucaram told reporters at Buenos Aires airport.
Ecuador's Congress deposed Bucaram last week on grounds of "mental incapacity." Bucaram has challenged the legislature's constitutional authority to take such a move.
Congress's leader, Fabian Alarcon, has been sworn in as interim president until new elections are held next year.
Bucaram was scheduled to meet with Argentine President Carlos Menem. Menem is Bucaram's strongest supporter in the region.
On Wednesday, Menem said Alarcon is leading a "de facto" government and he instructed Argentine diplomats in Quito not to attend the inauguration.
Bucaram, who was accompanied by one of his sons, said: "Nobody beat me in an election. Four people cannot ruin a constitution in a minute."
